# 2 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The Jews of Jerusalem and of Judea, and the council of elders, and Judas — to our brothers the Jews throughout Egypt: greetings and good peace.

**2** May God be gracious to you, and may he remember his covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, his faithful servants.

**3** May he give to all of you a heart to worship him and to do his will with a strong heart and a willing soul.

**4** May he open your hearts to his law and his commandments, and may he grant you peace.

**5** May he hear your prayers and be reconciled to you, and may he not abandon you in the time of evil.

**6** And now here we are, praying for you.

**7** In the reign of Demetrius, in the one hundred and sixty-ninth year, we Jews wrote to you in the pressing distress that came upon us in those years, from the time when Jason and his associates apostatized from the holy land and the kingdom,

**8** and they burned the gateway and shed innocent blood. Then we prayed to the LORD and were heard, and we offered sacrifice and grain offering; and we lit the lamps and we set out the bread of the Presence.

**9** And now take care to observe the days of the Festival of Booths in the month of Chislev.

**10** In the one hundred and eighty-eighth year — the people in Jerusalem and Judea, the council of elders, and Judas, to Aristobulus, who is the teacher of King Ptolemy and who is of the family of the anointed priests, and to the Jews in Egypt — greetings and health.

**11** Having been rescued by God from grave dangers, we offer him great thanks, since we took the field against a king such as that.

**12** For it was he who drove out those who had arrayed themselves against the holy city.

**13** For when the general arrived in Persia with an army that seemed invincible, they were cut down in the temple of Nanea by the treachery of Nanea's priests.

**14** For Antiochus came to the place with his Friends, on the pretense of marrying her, in order to receive the large amounts of money called dowry.

**15** When the priests of Nanea had set out the money and Antiochus had come with a small group within the sacred precinct, the priests closed the temple as soon as he entered.

**16** Opening the secret trapdoor in the ceiling, they pelted the leader and his companions with stones. They cut the men to pieces and threw the heads to those standing outside.

**17** Blessed in all things be our God, who has handed over those who acted impiously.

**18** Since on the twenty-fifth day of Chislev we shall celebrate the purification of the temple, we considered it necessary to notify you, in order that you also may celebrate the festival of booths and the festival of the fire given when Nehemiah, who built the temple and the altar, offered sacrifices.

**19** For when our ancestors were being taken to Persia, the pious priests of that time took some of the fire of the altar and secretly hid it in the hollow of a dry cistern, where they kept it safe so that the place was unknown to anyone.

**20** After many years had passed, when it pleased God, Nehemiah, having been commissioned by the king of Persia, sent the descendants of the priests who had hidden the fire to recover it. When they reported to us that they had found no fire, but only thick liquid,

**21** he ordered them to draw it out and bring it to him. When the sacrifices had been set in order, Nehemiah commanded the priests to sprinkle the wood and what was placed upon it with that liquid.

**22** When this had been done and some time had elapsed, and when the sun that had been hidden by clouds shone out, a great fire blazed up, so that all were filled with wonder.

**23** While the sacrifice was being consumed, the priests prayed — with Jonathan leading and the rest responding, as Nehemiah did too.

**24** The prayer was as follows: "O LORD God, Creator of all things, you who are awesome and strong and righteous and merciful, you who alone are King and gracious,

**25** you who alone provide for all, you who alone are just and almighty and eternal, you who rescue Israel from every evil, who made our ancestors your chosen ones and consecrated them:

**26** accept this sacrifice for all your people Israel and preserve your heritage and make it holy.

**27** Gather together our scattered people, free those who are enslaved among the Gentiles, look with favor on those who are rejected and despised, and let the nations know that you are our God.

**28** Punish those who oppress and treat us with insolence.

**29** Plant your people in your holy place, as Moses proclaimed."

**30** Then the priests sang the hymns.

**31** After the sacrifice was consumed, Nehemiah ordered the remaining liquid to be poured on large stones.

**32** When this was done, a flame blazed up, but was extinguished by the light shining back from the altar.

**33** When the matter became known and it was reported to the king of Persia that, in the place where the exiled priests had hidden the fire, water had appeared, with which Nehemiah and his associates had purified the sacrificial materials,

**34** the king investigated the matter, had the place enclosed, and declared it sacred.

**35** To those with whom the king exchanged gifts, he gave them in generous amounts.

**36** Nehemiah and his associates called this thing "Nephthar," which is translated "purification," but most people call it "naphtha."
